figures.shows: The Open World sample's central rock face and the grass below it, seen across the sea from about 1.3 km, with the height fog off, under aerial perspective off, on at scale 1, and on at scale 6
figures.caption: The island's central rock face and grass, 1.3 km away, with the height fog off; in order: haze off, scale 1, scale 6. At scale 6 the rock turns a cool gray and the grass bluer.
figures.numbers: 1.3 km is the camera's distance to the rock face (the camera stands at 900, 20, 900 and looks at 28, 48, -28, near the island's center at the origin); six is the scale-6 variant's AerialPerspectiveScale.
figures.alt: One of three pictures of an island's rock face and grass: haze off, scale 1, scale 6. At scale 6 the rock and grass turn bluer.

figures.shows: The Open World sample's island peak seen across the water, the sun to the right outside the frame, under the Atmosphere sky (Clear preset) at sun elevations of 60, 20, 6, 0 and -6 degrees; the command reports the ground's illuminance as about 103,100, 82,500, 41,900, 1,770 and 0 lux
figures.caption: The sun stands at 60°, 20°, 6°, 0° and −6°. As it sinks, its light turns from white to red and the sky from blue to violet. At −6° the glow is twilight, not sunlight. Automatic exposure brightens each picture, so they show color, not the fall of light.
figures.numbers: The elevations are the variants' sunElevation (sun-60, sun-20, sun-6, sun-0, sun-minus-6, in the page's order); the illuminances are the groundIlluminance that lighting.applySkyPreset reported for each variant in the take (103,100, 82,538, 41,859, 1,770 and 0 lux), rounded.
figures.alt: One of five pictures of the same island peak across water. At 60 degrees the sky is blue and the rock and grass are lit white. At 20 only the horizon pales. At 6 the peak is golden. At 0 it is orange-red under a purple sky, and at minus 6 a soft red under a violet sky.
